name: What Your Chrome Remembers
creator: Ensemble broadcast: Tobias Achike-Svensson, Preet Molnár-Oduya, 'DJ Lacunae' (anonymous)
description: A music criticism and culture podcast focused entirely on the intersection of neural-feed music distribution, BCI-mediated listening experiences, and the underground sound scenes that refuse corporate neural distribution channels. The three hosts approach music from radically different positions — Achike-Svensson is an academic musicologist, Molnár-Oduya is a Tier 2 club promoter, and the anonymous DJ Lacunae speaks from somewhere in the Gray Zone underground scene — and their arguments are as much of the show as their analysis. Physical media, pirate frequency music, and the Ghost Frequency underground scene receive particular attention.
medium: neural feed audio / audio stream / occasional physical cassette editions
cultural_impact: The show is one of the primary critical venues through which the Gray Zone and underground music reaches Tier 3 audiences, functioning as a kind of cross-tier cultural translation service that neither sanitizes its sources nor exoticizes them.
controversy: DJ Lacunae's continued anonymity has generated years of speculation; a 2215 episode in which she described a specific the Gray Zone location in unusual detail led to a brief period of intense doxing attempts by corporate media outlets, which the other hosts publicly condemned.
story_hooks: DJ Lacunae announces she is going to reveal her identity on an upcoming episode — and then the episode never comes, and she stops responding to the other hosts.
The show receives a recording of a piece of music that appears to have been composed by a non-human intelligence; none of the hosts can agree on what it is or where it came from.

A corporate label begins releasing music that sounds almost identical to underground the Gray Zone artists the show has covered — close enough to be suspicious, different enough to avoid infringement claims.
